scenes.heading: HCF and LCM in problems
scenes.sub: The biggest tile? The next time the lights flash together?
scenes.say: What is the biggest square tile that fits a floor exactly? When will three flashing lights flash together again? These are H C F and L C M problems. In this video you will learn a fast prime-factor method, and how to tell which one a problem needs.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Numbers built from prime Lego bricks: 72 = three 2s and two 3s
scenes.science: HCF: smaller pile of each prime. LCM: bigger pile.
scenes.breaks: Real Lego can use any brick; a number’s prime bricks are fixed and unique.
scenes.say: Think of each number as a Lego model built from prime bricks. Seventy-two is three twos and two threes. For the H C F, build only with bricks both numbers share, taking the smaller pile of each prime. For the L C M, you need enough bricks to build either number, so take the bigger pile.

scenes.heading: Lowest powers or highest powers?
scenes.say: Seventy-two is two cubed times three squared. One hundred and twenty is two cubed times three times five. The H C F uses common primes at their lowest powers: twenty-four. The L C M uses every prime at its highest power: three hundred and sixty.

scenes.heading: The product rule (two numbers)
scenes.say: For any two numbers, the H C F times the L C M equals the two numbers multiplied together. Twenty-four times three hundred and sixty is eight thousand six hundred and forty, and so is seventy-two times one hundred and twenty.
scenes.caption: HCF × LCM = a × b

scenes.heading: Tiling a floor
scenes.question: A 360 cm by 264 cm floor: largest square tiles, no cutting. How many?
scenes.say: The largest tile that fits both sides exactly is the H C F of three hundred and sixty and two hundred and sixty-four, which is twenty-four centimetres. Fifteen tiles fit along one side and eleven along the other, so you need one hundred and sixty-five tiles.

scenes.heading: Flashing lights
scenes.question: Lights flash every 12, 18 and 30 seconds. When together again?
scenes.say: Together again means L C M. Using the highest powers, two squared times three squared times five is one hundred and eighty seconds. The lights flash together every three minutes.

points: Groups, tiles → HCF; together again → LCM
scenes.say: Remember: H C F uses common primes at the lowest powers. L C M uses all primes at the highest powers. For two numbers, H C F times L C M is their product. Groups and tiles need the H C F; together again needs the L C M. Now try the practice questions!
